title: Drag a file into the green folder on a computer screen with a real mouse
instruction: Using the mouse, drag the red file into the green folder on the screen, then let go of the mouse.
context: Dragging a file into a folder with a mouse is an everyday task for most people. For a robot the hard part is the hand: 1 mm of mouse travel moves the pointer 31.5 pixels, so the drop must land within about 2 mm of travel, while the button stays held through the move and the mouse stays flat on its mat, since a lifted sensor stops the pointer. The nearest task elsewhere is the DexJoCo suite's 'Click Mouse', which sets a mouse on its pad and clicks it; here the button is held through a drag, and the file is landed on a folder within about 2 mm of mouse travel by watching the on-screen pointer. One arm can do it; two are allowed.
setup: Two YAM arms at the near edge of a table; positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y left) in cm, heights above the table. A 24-inch 1920 x 1080 monitor (picture 53.1 x 29.9 cm, black housing with 0.9 cm bezels and a 2 cm chin) on a grey stand with a 17 x 24 cm foot, its picture's bottom edge at x 57, centred on y 0, 4.5 cm up, leaned back 20 degrees. The desktop has a dark blue wallpaper; along its top, four folder icons 150 px across (4.2 cm on the panel), their centres 250 px from the top and 420, 780, 1140 and 1500 px from the left, coloured blue, green, yellow and purple with the desktop's folder-colour option, in an order set by the seed; a red document icon, 110 x 140 px, in the lower part of the screen; and the pointer at a large accessibility size, about 145 px tall. The file's and the pointer's places are set by the seed. On a dark cloth mouse mat, 24 cm along x by 26 cm along y and 3 mm thick, centred at (34, -13), a wireless optical mouse, 116 x 62 x 38 mm and 85 g, matte dark grey plastic on PTFE feet, its left button clicking at 0.6 N after 0.4 mm of travel. The mouse starts within 2 cm of the mat's centre along each axis, turned up to 8 degrees, by seed. The mat is taped to the table. Pointer speed: 31.5 px per mm of mouse travel (a 1,600 cpi sensor at a 0.5 multiplier), acceleration off. The screenshot shows seed 1.
scoring: Read from a screen recording and a video of the table and hands, in sync. The file goes into a folder when the button comes up while the file is being dragged (it has moved 6 px or more with the button held on it) and the pointer's tip is on that folder's icon (150 x 128 px). 1.0 when the file is in the green folder, the button is up, every finger is at least 1 cm from the mouse, and the mouse is on its mat and upright (tilted 30 degrees or less), held for 1 s. 0.5 when the file is in the green folder but that end state is not held for 1 s. 0.25 when the file has been let go on the desktop with its centre at most half as far, in a straight line, from the green folder's centre as at the start. 0 otherwise. 0 also if at any moment the file is dropped into another folder, a folder is dragged, a folder or the file is opened by a double click (two clicks within 0.5 s and 10 px), the mouse leaves its mat (its centre goes past the mat's edge, or it tilts over 30 degrees; lifting it level over the mat is allowed), or a finger touches the monitor.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Move the file back out of the folder to its start, and set the folders' order and the pointer's start for the seed, by hand or with a short script. Set the mouse on the mat. Before trials, check the pointer speed: with acceleration off and the pointer near the screen's left edge, slide the mouse 50 mm to the right along a ruler; the pointer must move 1,575 px.
fidelity: Rigid-body physics at 240 Hz on GPU. The mouse is a free body; its left button is a sprung shell (1,500 N/m, a 0.6 mm stop), closing at 0.4 mm (0.6 N) and opening when the press falls below 0.3 mm. The screen is drawn by code from the sensor: its motion in the mouse's own axes times 31.5 px per mm, counted only within 1.5 mm of the mat; a drag starts after 6 px with the button held. Friction: feet on mat 0.15, fingertip on shell 0.6. No mouse cable.
